Resolves #18033

The dock series explained the architecture, the adoption decisions, the panes, the windows, the styling and the state — and left the landed product surface undocumented, so a developer had to search examples, tests and source to learn which capabilities exist and which are policy-controlled. This adds `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsFeatures.md`, a tour of that surface organized by user outcome, written by driving the running standalone example rather than by reading source and describing it.

Its spine is the distinction a reader needs first: features that commit through the reducer (and can therefore be refused, captured and replayed) versus features that only change what this window is showing (maximize, reveal, previews). R1 sharpened that line: a commit makes state *capturable*, not durable — persistence is the consumer's own capture/save/restore step, and the guide now says so and routes to the persistence guide. Two facts the source alone would have told wrong, both caught on the page: the pop-out action is enabled by default yet correctly absent wherever no runtime can produce a vessel, and a locked pane's header keeps its `unlock` because a pressed action leaves the focus gate — so you cannot lock yourself out of a pane.

Evidence: L3 achieved (live journeys on the running standalone dock example — real clicks, committed document read between steps; mermaid rendered and *measured* through the portal's own bundle) → L2 required (docs guide: link lint, tree registration, render verification, current-source consistency; no unit tests). Residual: none.

## Test Evidence

All of this is outside CI — a docs guide has no unit tier. Journeys ran on the standalone dock example at dev@474f4290c8, 1024 × 768, committed document read between every step:

- **Action rail, focus-gated.** Unfocused headers carried exactly one action (`close`); clicking into the Inspector header revealed `lock · reload · unpin · maximize · close`. Pop-out absent — `dockPopOutActionActive` requires a tear-out bundle and a vessel-capable realm, and the example composes neither.
- **Auto-hide round trip.** Header pin → the only document delta is `inspector.autoHidden: true`, nodes untouched → rail → click reveals a 256px overlay (the committed `extent: 0.25` of a 1024px viewport) whose right edge lands at 1010px, exactly the rail strip's left edge, painted over a projection that did not reflow → overlay pin commits `{autoHidden: false, pinned: true}`, same zone, same extent, same live component.
- **Lock.** `setItemLocked` → close hidden, `unlock` retained, `neo-dock-pane-locked` cue, one `inert` subtree (no pane implements the lock contract here). Sending `closeItem` to the reducer anyway returned `applied: false`, `errors: ['item "logs" is locked']`, document unchanged.
- **Resize.** `resizeSplit` moved `root-split` from `[0.65, 0.35]` to `[0.45, 0.55]`; nothing else in the document changed.
- **Maximize.** Node painted the workspace rect, `Escape` restored, and the committed document was byte-identical before and after.
- **Perspectives.** Selecting the second perspective restored both split ratios and the active tab and erased the lock and pin flags committed in between — the whole-document replacement the guide states as a limit.
- **Mermaid render.** The guide's fenced block was extracted to a file (sha256 `5a02ad4b9b8a…`), and the string rendered in the browser hashed identically, so the rendered artifact is the file's diagram and not a retyped copy. Rendered through the portal's own `dist/mermaid.mjs`: 36 166-byte SVG, 29 nodes, 18 links, no error icon. Negative control along the same path (deliberately broken syntax) returned a parse error and 0 bytes, so the reader can fail.
- **Portal page render.** The harness dev server resolves to the primary checkout rather than this worktree, so the new page could not be loaded there; the portal's guide-render path was instead proven on `DockLayoutsMechanics` along the identical route (20 427 chars, 1 SVG). Full-page render of this guide is listed below for post-merge.

**R1 repairs at `ea98d54b50`.** The diagram was rebuilt around the committed-versus-transient story alone (the operation-name catalog moved into the prose beneath it) and re-measured through the portal's own `dist/mermaid.mjs` at the 597px content column @neo-gpt-emmy measured: **viewBox width 1575.33 → 704.74, scale 0.379 → 0.847, effective label size 6.1px → 13.55px**, 19 node elements, 10 links, no error. Two iterations — the first revision reached only 9.91px and was rejected on its own measurement. Each rendered string was hash-checked against the file's fenced block (`91c279869dc8…`) so the measured artifact is the committed diagram. `check-relative-links` re-run: OK, 233 links across 166 files.

**The full-page render residual is closed, by the reviewer.** @neo-gpt-emmy served the exact PR Markdown and `learn/tree.json` to the existing portal renderer on an isolated local server: at 1300×1000 the page carried the opening and final sections, 25,350 characters of rendered text, one SVG, zero page errors — the new guide, not a sibling. That is the receipt my own environment could not produce, and it is what turned RA-3 from a suspicion into a measurement.
